newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech Synthesia sees 96 profit despite 9mo loss.
newsitem.headline: Czech Synthesia sees 96 profit despite 9mo loss.

text.p: Czech chemical concern Synthesia a.s., maker of the plastic explosive Semtex, said it expected to post a profit in 1996 despite showing a loss for the first nine months, a company spokesman said on Monday.
"We expect a positive result, but it is too soon for an analysis of the reasons," Synthesia spokesman Ales Mokren told Reuters declining to specify an approximate profit forecast.
He added that Synthesia, which makes mainly chemicals and paints, "would most probably" not pay a dividend in 1996, following its no dividend policy of previous years.
For the nine month period ending September 30, the company posted a loss of 35.3 million crowns, down from a gross profit of 288.7 million for the same period in 1995.
In 1995 the company posted gross profit of 127 million crowns and a net profit of 83.35 million, down from 351.77 million in 1994.
Semtex, a brand of plastic explosive favoured by guerrillas worldwide, accounts for only about 0.01 percent of the firm's total revenues.
It comes in red, orange or black blocks like children's modelling clay and is perhaps the Czech Republic's best-known product after beer, although the makers have mixed feelings about its fame.
The explosive has been linked with a string of terrorist attacks, including the 1988 bombing of PanAm flight 103 that killed 270 people.
